setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: Named by the rep at the open despite no setter suffix in the title: 'I already got some information from Kim, could be that I ask the same questions just because I want to get the whole picture clear.' He drew on her notes repeatedly — 'I also heard that you're having sort of bad posture at work because you have a desk job' and 'I also saw, of course, you sort of noted down that you want to have longevity and energy.'

prospect.name: James
prospect.occupation: Works in financial management and the financial markets, building his own venture and currently drawing no reliable income. Sixteen years in corporate sales previously. Has a desk-based working pattern.
prospect.family_status: Single father of two young children with roughly 50/50 custody, alternating two- and three-day blocks
prospect.training_background: Ran seriously for several years — a couple of marathons and around a dozen half marathons. Worked with a personal trainer five or six years ago. Fitness went entirely to the back burner through COVID and two children, reaching about 200 lb. Three months before this call he started a structured calisthenics programme four times a week in a 200-400 calorie deficit, has lost 20 lb, taken daily steps from around 4,000 to 11,000, and progressed dips from bench variations to four sets of five bodyweight reps. Describes the change as an identity shift rather than a diet. Has never used kettlebells and has no confidence with them.
prospect.medical: A cascading back injury sequence beginning when he lifted his son into a crib — mid back went out, then the lower back, then neck and shoulders, each area compensating for the last. Around a year of physiotherapy followed. He believes it is now resolved through physio plus dedicated back strengthening, but is explicitly unsure: 'who knows if I'm on thin ice there.' Currently reports soreness at the left elbow which he attributes to connective tissue rather than joint — 'I feel like that could be one thing that goes if I continue this progression.' Rounded shoulders and the beginning of a hump from desk work. Also self-reports chronically poor energy, improving during the deficit. No clinician was consulted about kettlebell training and no clearance was sought.

signals: Opened with the archetype's exact framing, unprompted: 'I'm at a good place, just want to take it to the next level'
Already succeeding under his own steam — 20 lb down, 11,000 steps a day, three months of unbroken consistency, and a documented strength progression he tracks himself
Refused on liquidity rather than on value, and said so explicitly: 'the bang for your buck is probably there... it's just too much for me at the moment'
Buying planning and expertise rather than motivation — his stated need is what to do in phase two, how long to cut, and kettlebell form, not accountability
Departs from the archetype on one clause: price is not a quality signal here but a genuine barrier, because he is between incomes and living off runway while building a business

goals.text: Finish the current cut and know how to transition into a lean bulk — 'not sure what to do to get to that next phase'
Lose the remaining stomach fat and stop being skinny fat
Build lean muscle into a V taper — lats, shoulders, delts, tighter stomach
Learn correct kettlebell form, having zero confidence with the modality
Correct rounded shoulders and the beginning of a hump from desk work
Improve energy, which he describes as chronically terrible and only recently improving
Be functional and active with two young children
Longevity understood as staying functional with high energy rather than getting big
Avoid another injury, which he names as the only thing that could stop him
Make the change permanent — 'it would feel like a lifestyle and identity shift'
Have the structure and planning for phase two rather than guessing

pains.text: A year of cascading back injuries requiring physiotherapy, with each area compensating and failing in turn; unsure whether he is still 'on thin ice'
Active left elbow soreness he attributes to connective tissue and fears will fail if he keeps progressing
No income at present while building a new venture, living off 12-15 months of runway
In the guessing stage on programming — does not know when to stop cutting, whether to maintain, or how to lean bulk
Zero confidence with kettlebells and no idea about form or routine
Historical pattern of hitting a plateau in gym routines and giving up
Chronically poor energy, only recently and partially improving
Rounded shoulders and posture degradation from a desk job
Irrational impatience with three months of progress — 'I expect it more after three months, which is a crazy thought because it's just not realistic'
Single parenting two young children on a 50/50 schedule constrains when he can train

objections.raw_quote: I don't know if I want to drop a chunk upfront. So I don't know if that would be a detriment. I don't think I want to drop that significant amount upfront.
objections.rep_response: Isolated cleanly — 'is it like, it's too much, I just cannot afford it at the moment? is it mainly just a certainty aspect?' — and ran the hypothetical: 'let's say 9K Canadian would now fall on your lap, would you be like, okay, Richard, let's get started', answered 'Oh, yeah, yeah, yeah.' Then offered an in-house six-payment plan at an extra $200 a month.

objections.raw_quote: here's my situation, right? Like, I'm not working at the moment, right? So I have money that I'm living off of as I build like this kind of new business... I wasn't expecting to drop an extra thousand bucks a month right now.
objections.rep_response: Acknowledged it and did not push, saying he would rather the prospect not buy than be put in a difficult financial position. Pressed once on whether delay actually helps — 'when it comes to doing like sort of the waiting another 60 days, when do you know when to stop cutting?' — then improvised a first-month opt-out to reduce the commitment.

objections.raw_quote: give me the time to think about, do your follow-ups... so do your follow-ups, I suspect you will, but I'm going to sit on it, I am interested, but I am going to sit on it just due to the investment right now.
objections.rep_response: Ran the deciding-versus-thinking move — 'do you really think that thinking about is going to make a big difference or is it going to boil down to seeing how you could make it work?' — which returned 'It's going to boil down to seeing how I can make it work.' The prospect, a sixteen-year sales veteran, then named the technique out loud: 'you're doing your role now and you're doing your role against someone who's done it for you know 20 years.' The rep backed off and agreed a bi-weekly nurture cadence.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Quoted live: 'we can for now split up into six payments in house, basically, that would come with an extra $200 a month for processing fees, etc.' Six instalments of roughly $1,200 against a $6,000 offer, a total of $7,200 with the $1,200 uplift attributed to processing fees. Third-party financing was offered and declined. Early settlement was offered — paying the balance off would remove the remaining $200 monthly additions. The rep additionally improvised a first-month exit: 'we also have a [try] it or leave it... if you don't feel like after a month... you don't really see the results, you don't really see the benefits, we can stop it. But with the idea to continue for the rest of the five months, and that would just be the first monthly payment.'
offer.guarantee_mentioned: Stated conditionally: 'if you do everything correctly, like how you should be doing it, and we haven't seen the progress of at least getting to being more ripped right and having that longevity aspect for yourself, then Trevor does continue coaching you.' Followed by 'I'm like 99% sure that that's not going to happen' and 'we are 100% going to go past your goals.'

evidence: No payment taken, no payment link sent, and no onboarding booked.
Explicit deferral with stated interest: 'I'm going to sit on it, I am interested, but I am going to sit on it just due to the investment right now.'
Confirmed at the end: 'I am interested. The timing is just not right for me. It really boils down to that... Just put me in your nurture list.'
Value was not the blocker and he said so twice — 'I think the bang for your buck is probably there. It's just, it's just too much for me at the moment.'
A concrete follow-up cadence was agreed: bi-weekly check-ins by email or text, with the prospect to message the rep directly if he decides to proceed.

Counter-evidence pointing to a genuinely live deal: he rated the programme 'an easy seven' out of ten before price, confirmed he would start immediately if the money were there, and said the improvised first-month exit and early-settlement options 'would help me sign off when the timing is right'. Trigger for reactivation is his new venture producing income, which he put at anywhere from days to 90 days.
outcome.next_step: Bi-weekly email or text nurture from the rep; prospect to message directly when his business income allows. Rep to send occasional community updates.

notable.note: Three commercial findings on one call. The instalment plan was quoted at an extra $200 a month described as processing fees, which takes a $6,000 offer to $7,200 — the same total this rep reached on 06/29 by a different route. The rep then improvised a first-month opt-out that exists nowhere in the offer, and the prospect confirmed it would move his decision. And asked for anything written describing what six months and $6,000 actually buys, the rep had nothing: 'Actually, we don't really have it written out, to be honest.' Separately, the prospect independently confirmed the publicly advertised $199 a month price is anchoring buyers — 'I think I saw on your site that you do, like, $1.99 a month... maybe that's why I had that number in my head' — which the rep acknowledged and explained he had chosen not to offer. This is the call reviewed in the coaching one-to-one an hour later, where the manager's notes concerned only the pitch; none of the pricing improvisation, the missing collateral or the injury history was raised.

quality.notes: Heavy inversion throughout, including several multi-minute stretches where both sides of an exchange sit under one label — most severely from 00:00:40 to 00:02:47, where the rep's opening question and the prospect's entire first answer run together under the prospect, and again from 00:15:33 to 00:16:00 and 00:41:27 to 00:41:42 where the payment-plan discussion alternates within single blocks. All roles resolved from content. Age and weight are recovered from the rep's recap at 00:19:58 rather than from a direct question. Body fat is recorded at 26 as the midpoint of the prospect's own '25, 27' estimate from a gym body-composition machine in December, before the 20 lb loss, so it is stale. Transcription noise includes 'Fathrite' and 'Fath' for fat, 'feed taper' for V taper, and 'a of it or leave it' for what is clearly 'a try it or leave it'.
